A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Intent3D dataset and IntentNet method. All 22 pages in each version, including equations, figures, tables, and supplementary Sections 7–11, support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original Intent3D benchmark evaluations, component ablations, qualitative results, and a supplementary GPT-4 comparison in Tables 1–3 and 5.

after.justification: v2 retains the original benchmark evaluations, ablations, qualitative results, and supplementary GPT-4 comparison.

M1.justification: Section 4 retains the same architecture, Candidate Box Matching, Verb-Object Alignment, Cascaded Adaptive Learning, losses, and inference procedure. Changed citation numbers identify the same underlying methods.

E1.justification: Both use the same Intent3D coverage: 44,990 intention texts, 209 object classes, and 1,042 ScanNet scenes. The supplementary multiple-object and ambiguous-intention scenarios are also retained.

E2.justification: Tables 1–2 retain BUTD-DETR, EDA, 3D-VisTA, and zero-shot/fine-tuned Chat-3D-v2. Supplementary Table 5 retains the two-stage GPT-4 comparator. The newly cited works are not added to any evaluated comparison.

E3.justification: Both retain the 35,850/2,285/6,855 training/validation/test split, training settings, checkpoint selection by validation AP@0.5, and Top1-Accuracy/AP evaluation at IoU thresholds 0.25 and 0.5. Supplementary evaluation procedures also match.

E4.justification: Table 3 and Figure 5 retain the same component ablations. Supplementary Table 4 and Figures 6–7 retain the same generation failures, correct/incorrect predictions, and ambiguity case study.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run or seed counts, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests for the experimental comparisons. Both retain the same point-estimate reporting.

E6.justification: Numerical results, dataset statistics, rankings, and qualitative findings match throughout. For example, IntentNet's validation/test AP@0.5 remain 25.36/27.60, and the supplementary GPT-4 baseline's validation AP@0.5 remains 7.76.

T1.justification: The task definition, loss equations (1)–(3), and adaptive-loss formulation are unchanged. Neither version adds or removes formal assumptions, theorems, proofs, or derivations.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions: the 3D Intention Grounding task, Intent3D dataset, baseline evaluations, and IntentNet. Their novelty and performance claims have unchanged scope.

C2.justification: Interpretations of baseline performance and component effectiveness are retained. Supplementary discussions preserve the same limitations concerning GPT-4-generated data, multiple-target detection, annotation ambiguity, and subjective intentions.

D1.justification: Sections 5.2 and 7–8 retain the same hyperparameters, generation temperature, convergence epochs, and checkpoint instructions. The stated plan to release data, code, and checkpoints upon acceptance is also unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds five references: SegVG, ACTRESS, Visual Grounding with Attention-Driven Constraint Balancing, LLaVA-PruMerge, and LLM Inference Unveiled. They expand citation lists in Sections 1–2 without adding substantive comparisons or changing the novelty argument.

P1.justification: Citation markers throughout and the front-page arXiv version/date stamp are updated. The prose, terminology, section order, and organization of the main text and supplementary material otherwise remain unchanged.

P2.justification: The added references reflow the bibliography across pages 16–18 and cause limited paragraph line wrapping. Figures 1–7 and Tables 1–5 retain their displays, captions, structure, and placement, apart from updated citation numbers.

improvement.justification: v2 supplies five additional background references without expanding their discussion. The method, empirical evidence, explanations, reproducibility information, and supplementary limitations remain unchanged. The extra pointers and minor layout reflow produce no meaningful net difference in overall paper quality.
